clue.text: Plant producing birdseed?

parts.note: read whimsically, a young bird's pea would be seed for a bird, and that pulse is a real plant

explanation.surface: A plant grown to supply seed for the aviary.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful reading: split the answer into a baby bird and a pea and you have seed fit for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The garbanzo is a leguminous plant whose seeds are eaten as pulses.

clue.text: Maximum content of policy on Liverpool, for instance?

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece on top of the second

parts.note: CAP is the EU's Common Agricultural Policy
Liverpool is an example of a city in England

explanation.surface: How much an insurance policy covers in Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: CAP is the Common Agricultural Policy; Liverpool is A CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: The most that a container or space can hold is its volume or limit.

clue.text: Arrogant spirit in Finland has been overthrown

indicators.note: in puts the spirit inside the overthrown country name
overthrown in a down clue means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: Suomi is Finland's name for itself
a peri is a fairy or spirit of Persian myth

explanation.surface: A haughty ghost in Finland has been toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'has been overthrown' means read upwards, so Finland's own name turns into IMOUS before the spirit goes 'in'. A peri is a fairy of Persian myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Domineering and haughty, expecting obedience from others.

clue.text: Dog off colour in Ireland

indicators.note: off means the colour is taken away from the breed's name

parts.note: the Kerry blue is an Irish terrier breed
blue is a colour

explanation.surface: A hound looks unwell somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off colour' looks like 'unwell' but means drop a colour: the Kerry blue terrier loses BLUE. The result is a county in the southwest of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A county in the southwest of the Irish Republic, around Tralee and Killarney.

clue.text: Deed to take advantage of

explanation.surface: An act of using someone unfairly.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a bold feat; as a verb, to use something or someone for profit.

clue.text: Almost the best location for capital in Greece or Egypt

indicators.note: almost means the phrase stops just short of its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, then cut short; the run of letters it gives is shortened, not hidden, so the forward match is a coincidence of the device

explanation.surface: A place nearly the finest for a capital city, whether Greek or Egyptian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the final T of THEBEST. Both Greece and Egypt had an ancient city of this name, the Egyptian one a capital of the pharaohs.
explanation.definitionFit: Two ancient cities bore the name: one in Boeotia and one on the Nile, seat of the pharaohs.

clue.text: Hid garden items — like a broomsuck?

indicators.note: items treats the letters as separate pieces to be laid out afresh

explanation.surface: Things concealed in the garden, like a witch's broom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'items' rearranges HID GARDEN. A broomstick is literally ridden by a hag (witch); the word usually means tormented.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch's broom is mounted and flown by a crone, so it is literally hag-ridden, a word otherwise meaning tormented.

clue.text: Fish in Bucks

explanation.surface: A fish found in a Buckinghamshire stream.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks is Buckinghamshire, an English county; Brill is a village there.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatfish related to the turbot; also a hilltop village in Buckinghamshire.

clue.text: Drunk three of these in the monsoon, perhaps

definitions.text: Drunk three of these in the monsoon, perhaps

parts.words: Drunk three of these in the monsoon, perhaps
parts.note: a drunk is said to be three of these to the wind, and monsoon rain comes down in them

explanation.surface: Getting tipsy during the rainy season.
explanation.walkthrough: Two idioms: 'three ___ to the wind' means very drunk, and heavy rain falls in ___.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad flat expanses, of sailcloth ropes in the drinking idiom or of falling rain.

clue.text: Plough that can be repaired with traveller's help

annotationWithheld.why: Plough that can be repaired with traveller's help (6): the definition 'Plough' fits ARABLE but no parse of 'that can be repaired with traveller's help' gives the letters
annotationWithheld.clue: Plough that can be repaired with traveller's help

clue.text: Old German rat-catcher has mole quietly included

indicators.note: included tells us one piece is set inside the other here

parts.note: a mole is a harbour breakwater, a pier
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: An old German pest-controller has a burrowing mole slipped in quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: The mole is not the animal but a stone breakwater. The rat-catcher is the Pied Piper of Hamelin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pied Piper of Hamelin led the town's rats away with his music in the German legend.

clue.text: Archaic outlandish flyer

explanation.surface: A strange old-fashioned bird.
explanation.definitionFit: In old usage the word meant foreign or from abroad; it is also the name of a fast hunting falcon.

clue.text: Groom gets confused orders to implement

definitions.text: Groom gets confused orders to implement

parts.words: Groom gets confused orders to implement
parts.note: a stable groom is told both to curry and to comb a horse, and the two commands merge into the name of one tool

explanation.surface: A stable lad is given muddled instructions to carry out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Implement' looks like a verb (carry out) but is a noun, a tool. Curry and comb are both verbs for grooming a horse; mixed together they name the toothed grooming tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothed grooming tool for rubbing down horses and loosening dirt from the coat.

clue.text: Coastal feature gets state grant

parts.note: IN is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Indiana
to grant is to allow or let

explanation.surface: A seaside landform wins funding from the government.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow arm of the sea running into the land, a creek or small bay.

clue.text: "Language is the dress of — " (Johnson)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Samuel Johnson's Lives of the Poets, completed by the missing noun

explanation.surface: Complete Dr Johnson's saying about language.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson wrote that language is the dress of thought, meaning words clothe ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson's saying treats words as the clothing worn by ideas and reflection.

clue.text: Society for introduction of deer in Surrey

parts.note: a guild is a society or association

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An association for bringing deer into Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: Guildford is the county town of Surrey, south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The county town of the English county south-west of London.

clue.text: Church governors associate foreign articles with Saint

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
der is the German word for the

explanation.surface: Church officials link overseas items with a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: In Presbyterian churches lay office-holders who govern the congregation are called by this title.

clue.text: Hunter rushed to get bag on the QE

parts.note: ran means rushed
a sack is a bag
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A hunter hurried to fetch a bag aboard the liner Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.walkthrough: The QE looks like the ocean liner but stands for Queen Elizabeth, ER. A hunter here is one who searches through things.
explanation.definitionFit: One who searches thoroughly, rummaging through a place, is a seeker.

clue.text: Restored old shape of heavenly flower

indicators.note: restored means the old letters are put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A heavenly bloom brought back to its former form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restored' rearranges OLD SHAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this lily covered the Elysian fields, the paradise of the blessed dead.

clue.text: Strive to gain praise, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word praise is only one possible arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: Work hard to win acclaim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges PRAISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To strive towards something is to aim high or seek ambitiously to achieve it.

clue.text: Wit tries like mad to get round Philip I

indicators.note: to get round means the shuffled letters surround the other piece
like mad suggests the word tries goes wild
I, the Roman numeral one, asks for the first letter of Philip

explanation.surface: A comedian works frantically to win over King Philip the First.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like mad' rearranges TRIES to ESRIT, which goes 'round' P, the first letter of Philip (I, number one).
explanation.definitionFit: French for spirit, used in English for lively intelligence and sparkle.

clue.text: Crazy for fruit?

explanation.surface: Mad about fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for mad or wild with excitement; also the yellow tropical fruit in the plural.

clue.text: It's Jack's turn to clean out what's left

indicators.note: turn means the sailor's letters are flipped round

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, AB an able seaman
to lance a boil is to cut it open and clean it out

explanation.surface: A sailor takes his shift scrubbing up the leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' flips AB (able seaman, a jack tar) to BA, then LANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder, as with the sum left in an account after payments.

clue.text: Digital computer? It's a frame-up!

parts.note: a counting device worked by the fingers (digits), made of beads on a frame

explanation.surface: A computer joke that turns into a cry of being set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' means worked by fingers, not electronic; 'frame-up' is literal, beads strung on a frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A bead frame for doing sums by sliding counters with the fingers.

clue.text: Is trademark so new?

parts.note: a trademark is a mark on goods, and the same word joined to new makes the phrase for completely new

explanation.surface: A question about whether a logo is really that fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: The trademark sense gives the word, and 'so new?' points to the phrase meaning completely new, as in a newly made product.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade name or mark identifying a maker's goods, as in a well-known make.

clue.text: Articles about Frenchmen in Jordan

indicators.note: about means the articles wrap around the Frenchmen

parts.note: a and an are the indefinite articles
MM is messieurs, French for gentlemen

explanation.surface: Writings about French people in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: A and AN go 'about' MM (messieurs). The result is the capital of Jordan.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of the Hashemite Kingdom in the Middle East.

clue.text: College diagram used to detect true answer

parts.note: a poly was a polytechnic, a type of British college
a graph is a diagram plotting data

explanation.surface: A college chart employed to spot an honest reply.
explanation.walkthrough: A POLY was a British polytechnic college. The definition describes the lie detector by its use.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie detector records pulse and breathing to judge whether someone answers truthfully.

clue.text: Glut of Cheddar?.

explanation.surface: A surfeit of cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheddar is a Somerset village famous for its cheese and for Cheddar Gorge, a limestone ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff oneself greedily; also the ravine at the Somerset village of Cheddar.

clue.text: in turn it has nothing in common with agitation

indicators.note: in places one group of letters inside the word common

parts.note: taken as written
O is the round figure for nothing

indicators.note: in turn means the little word it is flipped round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A turn of phrase saying commotion and agitation share nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening lower-case 'in turn' is the reversal signal, making TI; the second 'in' is the container. 'with' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A commotion is a noisy disturbance, a state of turmoil and confusion.

clue.text: Hogarthian character's daughter is sternly inclined

parts.note: Hogarth's painting series A Rake's Progress follows a dissolute young man

explanation.surface: A figure from a Hogarth print has a daughter who is strict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sternly' is not 'strictly' but 'at the stern': a ship's stern or a mast that is raked slopes back.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's stern or mast that slopes backwards from the vertical is said to have this slant.

clue.text: Returning party to New York by ship for conventions

indicators.note: by ship is read as carried within a steamship, so the ship's letters go around the rest

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: returning sends the party and the city back to front together

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Heading home from a party in New York aboard a liner, bound for meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns the party and the city together into YNOD, and 'by ship' is read as aboard a steamship, so those letters sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Church councils or assemblies of clergy meeting formally are a kind of convention.

clue.text: Brainy monk in church with genuine following

indicators.note: following puts the genuine piece after the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: in tells us the monk is placed within the church and its follower

parts.note: real means genuine
Br is the abbreviation for brother, a title for a monk

explanation.surface: A clever friar in a church that is the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: A monk is addressed as Brother; that abbreviation sits inside the genuine piece, after the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Intellectual and highly rational, appealing to the intellect rather than the emotions.
